title: The people of the thick trees also did wrong.
subtitle: Shuayb's people, the dwellers of Al-Aykah
then: Ibn Kathir says the dwellers of Al-Aykah, meaning intertwined trees, were the people of Shuayb. {trap}Their evildoing included shirk, banditry and cheating in weights and measures{/trap}. They lived near Lut's people, at a later time.
now: You round the invoice up a little. You sell the phone without mentioning the cracked camera. You pad your hours. {trap}Small cheats in the scale.{/trap} {idea}This verse puts dishonest trade beside shirk.{/idea}
old: Business is business; a little rounding up hurts no one.
new: Cheating in a deal is a real wrong that Allah lists alongside the biggest ones.
try: Check one transaction, invoice or sale you have open and make it completely honest.

title: Two ruined towns, both on a road you can see.
subtitle: Lut and Shuayb, side by side
then: Ibn Kathir says Shuayb's people knew about Lut's people, which is why both are {idea}on an open route, plain to see{/idea}. Shuayb warned them in 11:89, {trap}the people of Lut are not far off from you{/trap}. They had a lesson next door and ignored it.
now: Your neighbor lost his family to the same temper you have. Your colleague got fired for the same shortcuts you take. {trap}It is easy to think it was just them.{/trap} {idea}The lesson is not far off from you.{/idea}
old: What happened to them will not happen to me.
new: When I see someone fall nearby for a habit I share, it is a warning addressed to me.
try: Think of one person who fell for something you also struggle with, and change one thing today.

title: Deny one messenger and you have denied them all.
subtitle: The people of Al-Hijr, which names this surah
then: This verse gives the surah its name. Ibn Kathir says the dwellers of Al-Hijr were Thamud, who rejected Salih, and {idea}whoever denies even one Messenger has disbelieved in all of them{/idea}. That is why it says messengers, plural.
now: You accept the parts of faith that are easy, prayer on Fridays, charity at Ramadan. The parts that cost you, you quietly skip. {idea}Guidance comes as one message.{/idea} Rejecting the hard parts is rejecting the source.
old: I can take the parts of the message that suit me.
new: The message is one whole; rejecting part of it means rejecting the One who sent it.
try: Name one part of your faith you avoid because it is hard, and take one small step toward it.

title: They saw the signs and turned their faces away.
subtitle: The she-camel from the rock

row.title: willingness
sub: they did not want to see

then: Ibn Kathir says Salih brought signs, {idea}like the she-camel Allah created for them out of solid rock{/idea}, which shared their water on alternate days. They killed it. He cites 41:17: {trap}they preferred blindness to guidance{/trap}.
now: Your doctor has shown you the scan three times. Your friend has shown you the bank statements. You still change the subject. {trap}It is not a lack of proof.{/trap} {idea}It is the turning away.{/idea}
old: If I had better proof, I would change.
new: Often the proof is already there; what is missing is my willingness to look at it.
try: Look honestly today at one piece of evidence you keep looking away from.

title: They carved homes in mountains and felt untouchable.
subtitle: Security built out of stone
then: Ibn Kathir says they had no real need for those houses; {trap}it was merely extravagance and work without a purpose{/trap}. When the Prophet ﷺ passed Al-Hijr on the way to Tabuk, {idea}he covered his head, hurried his camel, and told the Companions to pass only weeping{/idea}.
now: Bigger house, alarm system, investment portfolio, insurance on everything. {trap}It all says nothing can touch me.{/trap} {idea}Planning is fine. Feeling untouchable is the problem.{/idea}
old: With enough money and walls, I am safe.
new: No building or bank balance makes me secure; that feeling belongs to trust in Allah.
try: Next time you lock your door or check your savings, say: my safety is with Allah.

title: The stone did not stop the morning cry.
subtitle: The end of Thamud
then: After they killed the she-camel, Salih told them, {trap}enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days{/trap}, quoting 11:65. Ibn Kathir says the shriek overtook them {trap}in the morning of the fourth day{/trap}. The rock houses they trusted did not help.
now: You were told: three months to fix your health, or the job, or the marriage. You enjoyed the three months. {idea}A warning with a deadline is a gift.{/idea} Use the days you have.
old: I still have time before the warning comes true.
new: A warning with a deadline is mercy; the time given is for turning back, not for enjoying.
try: Pick one warning you have been given, by a doctor, a friend or your conscience, and act on it today.

title: Everything they earned could not help them.
subtitle: Crops, fruit, and water they would not share
then: Ibn Kathir explains: their crops, fruits, and {trap}the water which they did not want to share with the she-camel, so it would not reduce their share{/trap}, none of it protected them when their Lord's command came. They killed a sign of Allah over a share of water.
now: You argue with your sibling over who pays more for your mother's care. You refuse to share the parking spot, the inheritance, the credit. {trap}What you grip hardest may be what costs you most.{/trap}
old: Holding tight to what is mine keeps me safe.
new: What I refuse to share cannot save me, and may be exactly what brings me down.
try: Share something today you would normally keep for yourself: food, time, credit, or money.

title: The world has a purpose, so forgive beautifully.
subtitle: Created in truth, the Hour coming, forgive
then: Ibn Kathir says the heavens and earth were created with justice, and he cites 23:115: {idea}did you think We created you in play?{/idea} Then Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to {reward}overlook the faults of those who insulted him{/reward}. Mujahid and Qatadah said this was in Makkah, before fighting was prescribed.
now: Someone humiliated you in front of the family, and you have rehearsed the comeback for weeks. {idea}Nothing is wasted in a world made with truth.{/idea} {reward}You can forgive, beautifully, because justice is not your job alone.{/reward}
old: If I forgive them, they get away with it.
new: Because the world has a purpose and the Hour is coming, I can forgive without losing justice.
try: Choose one person who wronged you and forgive them today, without telling them or anyone.

title: The One who made everything knows every scattered piece.
subtitle: Your Lord, the Knowing Creator
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}a confirmation of the Day of Resurrection{/idea}. He knows {idea}what has been dispersed from people's bodies and scattered throughout the earth{/idea}. He cites 36:81: is not He who created the heavens able to create the like of them?
now: You forgave the person in the last verse, but it still feels like the wrong will just disappear. {idea}Your Lord made the heavens and knows every scattered thing.{/idea} {reward}Nothing you let go of is lost to Him.{/reward}
old: Once something is gone or forgotten, it is gone for good.
new: The Creator who knows every scattered piece can bring it all back and set it right.
try: Before sleeping, say ya Khallaq, ya Alim, and hand one worry over to Him.

title: You were given the Fatihah and the whole Quran.
subtitle: The seven oft-repeated verses
then: Scholars differed: some said the seven are the seven long surahs. Ibn Kathir cites Al-Bukhari, where the Prophet ﷺ called Al-Fatihah {reward}the most magnificent surah{/reward} and said {reward}it is the seven Mathani and the Grand Quran I have been given{/reward}.
now: You recite Al-Fatihah at least seventeen times a day, often on autopilot while thinking about lunch. {reward}It is the gift Allah named to comfort His Prophet ﷺ.{/reward} {idea}You already own the greatest treasure.{/idea}
old: Al-Fatihah is just the part I say quickly before the rest.
new: The seven verses I repeat every prayer are a gift Allah counted as immense.
try: In your next prayer, recite Al-Fatihah slowly, pausing after each verse.

title: Do not stare at what they have; be gentle with yours.
subtitle: Eyes off their luxuries, wings down for believers

row.title: what I was given
sub: the Quran, the people near me

then: Ibn Kathir says: since We gave you the Grand Quran, {idea}do not envy what they have of transient delights given to test them{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said this {trap}forbade a man to wish for what his companion has{/trap}. And be gentle with the believers, citing 9:128.
now: You scroll past a friend's new car, a cousin's holiday, a colleague's house. Then you snap at your own kids at dinner. {idea}Eyes off their things. Wings down for your people.{/idea}
old: If I had what they have, I would be happier.
new: I was given the Quran; I keep my eyes off others' luxuries and stay gentle with those near me.
try: Mute one account that makes you envious, and do one gentle thing for someone at home.
